title: Adversary trains on posterior samples, but the scored embedding is the posterior mean; at high λ the critic is satisfied while batch signal stays in the means (provisional)
description: Every adversary sees reparameterised samples z~q(z|x), the same choice as scvi-tools' AdversarialTrainingPlan. Every metric is computed on qz.loc. Batch information that sits below the posterior noise is therefore not penalised but stays in the scored representation. At fixed λ up to 30 (with no κ decay), the encoder can lower the adversary's loss by shrinking the means relative to σ, or by inflating σ, which the KL term rewards when σ<1. Neither removes batch structure from the means.
evidence: Source: scvi 1.4.2 _vaemixin.get_latent_representation returns qz.loc when give_mean=True (the default); AdversarialTrainingPlan.training_step uses inference_outputs['z']. DANN and WDGRL apply the adversary to the deterministic feature that is used downstream (WDGRL Alg. 1: h <- f_g(x)). Run (checks/gpu_checks_2.py: atac_small, SCVI conditioned, n_latent 10, batch 128, 12 epochs with KL warm-up shortened to 2, seed 0; PROVISIONAL). Balanced accuracy of a 3-fold logistic batch classifier on mean/sample (chance 0.333): λ=0 0.660/0.631; discriminator λ=20 0.425/0.409; reference λ=5 0.426/0.421; reference λ=30 0.708/0.440 (σ²/Var(μ) 0.80 vs 0.18 for λ=0; SD of means 0.375 vs 0.876); reference+zstd λ=30 0.860/0.420 (σ²/Var(μ) 1.89). At λ=30 the critic leaves more linearly decodable batch signal in the scored means than no adversary does.
reviewer_risk: Claims 1-2 (critic gives superior local mixing; critic over-corrects and collapses) can be explained by a mismatch between the representation that is trained and the one that is scored. A reviewer who decodes batch from the means will find batch signal left at high λ.
recommendation: Make the original Results §1 contrast rigorous by fixing what the adversary sees before the final run. Either (a) apply every adversary to qz.loc (the DANN/WDGRL-consistent choice), or to both the mean and a sample; or (b) keep samples but report every batch metric on both means and samples. Add a per-config masking diagnostic: batch decodability on the mean minus on the sample, plus σ²/Var(μ). Confirm this check on the stock schedule (2 datasets × 3 seeds) before running the 8-dataset benchmark. Over-correction is supported only if means show low batch decodability together with lost bio structure.

title: z-standardisation divides by one pooled RMS of sampled z: it removes only isotropic scale and opens two new shortcuts (provisional)
description: A single scalar RMS is computed per minibatch over all dimensions of the sampled z. (i) Anisotropy: inflating any batch-uninformative direction raises the RMS and shrinks the standardised batch differences, because standardised W1 is proportional to 1/RMS. (ii) Noise: raising posterior σ raises the RMS of the samples, and KL rewards this when σ<1. Neither shortcut costs the encoder much, so the arm does not remove the latent-scale shortcut it targets.
evidence: Algebra: for a batch shift δ along one axis, standardised W1 = δ/RMS with RMS² = mean_j Var(z_j). Same provisional run as N1, reference λ=30 with zstd vs without: posterior SD 0.71 vs 0.29; participation ratio of the latent means 2.65 vs 5.53 (λ=0: 7.68); top PC carries 0.57 of variance with batch η²=0.000; batch decodable from means 0.860 vs 0.708 (λ=0: 0.660).
reviewer_risk: The pilot is meant to show that the critics' behaviour is not a latent-scale artefact. As implemented, a zstd arm can reach low adversarial loss through a different artefact, so neither a null nor a positive pilot result can be interpreted.
recommendation: Inside the original hyperparameter-sensitivity section, standardise per dimension (or whiten) using statistics of the posterior means, and apply this to whatever the adversary sees (N1). Log the variance spectrum and σ²/Var(μ) for each config. Present zstd as a diagnostic arm, not a fix, unless its spectrum and masking gap match the λ=0 control.

title: The barycenter target is 64 learnable atoms started at the origin: they hardly move at small λ, and at large λ the latent contracts onto them (extends prior M2; provisional)
location: src/wcd_vae/wcd/adversarial.py:32,59 (n_anchors=64; anchors = randn*0.01); scripts/scvi_adversarial_plan.py:189-196 (anchors added to opt_g, which uses eps=self.eps=0.01)
description: (i) The target μ_A is an empirical measure on 64 points, so W1(P_k, μ_A) is at least the 64-point quantisation error of P_k. The loss can reach 0 only if each batch collapses onto at most 64 points or the latent shrinks: the objective has a degenerate minimiser by construction. (ii) The anchors start as a near point mass at 0 (SD 0.01) and are updated by the generator's Adam with scvi's eps=0.01, so their step is proportional to λ whenever |grad| < 0.01. Encoder and anchors minimise the same objective, so the encoder moves toward the anchors instead of the anchors moving to a barycenter of the batches.
evidence: Source: scvi 1.4.2 TrainingPlan eps default 0.01 (_trainingplans.py:154); AdversarialTrainingPlan does not override it. Run (checks/gpu_checks_1.py: atac_small, SCVI conditioned, batch 128, n_latent 10, 6 epochs, seed 0; PROVISIONAL): λ=0.01: anchor RMS 0.0099 -> 0.0117, median |grad| 4.8e-05, median step 4.7e-06 per step (lr 1e-3); anchor centroid 3.71 from the data centroid. λ=1: anchor RMS 0.14 vs latent RMS 0.77. λ=30: latent RMS 0.21 (vs 1.64 at λ=0.01), anchor RMS 0.22.
reviewer_risk: R2.5 asks whether the weakness comes from the reference design or from the Wasserstein objective. A barycenter arm whose target is a fixed point at small λ and a contracting 64-point quantiser at large λ cannot answer that question.
recommendation: Either make it a real barycenter, or drop it and answer R2.5 with reference vs pooled on K≥3 tasks (N4) plus a fixed-reference control (N5). A real barycenter needs: anchors initialised from encoded cells after a warm-up (e.g. k-means of pooled z); at least batch-size anchors; their own optimiser (eps 1e-8) or a closed-form free-support barycenter update; and anchor-vs-latent spread logged per epoch.

title: The pooled critic estimates (1−π_k)·W1(P_k, rest); with two batches it is exactly half the reference objective, and the choice of reference cannot matter
location: src/wcd_vae/wcd/critic.py:81 (pooled target_scores = output), :202 (GP ref_samples = z); src/wcd_vae/wcd/alignment.py mmd_batch_pool / sinkhorn_batch_pool (batch vs pool including its own cells)
description: By linearity, E_{P_k}C − E_pool C = (1−π_k)(E_{P_k}C − E_{P_−k}C), so each head estimates (1−π_k)·W1(P_k, P_−k). This down-weights large batches (head weight 0.22 for lung '10x v2', 0.25 for atac_large Fang), the opposite of the V-way cross-entropy/JS objective, which weights batch k by π_k; 'fair counterpart' is therefore not exact. For K=2 the pooled objective equals W1(P_1,P_2)/2, i.e. half the reference objective, and the reference objective is symmetric in which batch is the reference. A fraction π_k of each head's GP interpolates lie on within-batch segments. MMD against the pool scales as (1−π_k)².
evidence: Algebra above. Synthetic run with the repo's own head, GP and optimiser (checks/critic_estimator_check.py: two 10-D Gaussians, true W1=2, π=0.78/0.22): reference gap 2.22 (reference = batch 0) vs 2.23 (reference = batch 1); pooled head gaps 0.446 (expected 0.44) and 1.684 (expected 1.56); pooled objective 1.065 (expected 1.0). In the registry at 5709a98, lung and immune_hum_mou have K=2.
reviewer_risk: On 2-batch tasks, Results §4 (reference batch selection) and the reference-vs-pooled comparison carry no information: any reference effect there is estimator noise, and a reviewer can show this in one line.
recommendation: Keep the original reference-selection question but test it only on K≥3 tasks (scIB batch keys, N11), and state the K=2 equivalence in Methods. For pooled, either reweight heads by 1/(1−π̂_k) or define the target as the other batches (P_−k); report which. Describe the MMD/Sinkhorn targets the same way.

title: 'Reference' is not a fixed target: reference cells receive the summed pull of all K−1 heads
location: scripts/scvi_adversarial_plan.py:249-251 (generator step on non-detached z_adv); src/wcd_vae/wcd/critic.py forward
description: The generator gradient on a reference cell is −λ/(K−1)·(1/n_r)·Σ_{k≠r}∇C_k, so the reference batch is pushed K−1 times as hard in aggregate as any other batch (8× on pancreas). The objective is a star of symmetric pairwise W1 terms, not 'align onto a designated batch'.
evidence: Code reading of the gradient path: reference rows are not detached. WDGRL also lets both domains move through the shared extractor (Alg. 1), so co-moving is standard in domain adaptation, but it conflicts with the manuscript's 'align to a reference' framing.
reviewer_risk: Claim 3 ('the critic depends on a topologically dense reference') assumes the reference stays fixed. Reviewers will ask what is being aligned to what.
recommendation: Make claim 3 testable as worded: add a fixed-reference control (detach the z of reference cells in the generator step) on K≥3 tasks, and describe the default formulation as a star-shaped pairwise objective.

title: At batch size 128 each critic head sees only a few cells, and critics weight batches equally while the discriminator weights cells equally
location: src/wcd_vae/wcd/critic.py:92-123 (per-head means averaged over the heads present), :211-256 (per-head GP; absent heads skipped); scripts/scvi_adversarial_plan.py:272-278 (_fool_loss: per-cell mean)
description: Each head's gap and GP are estimated from the n_k cells of its batch in the minibatch, and a head is skipped when its batch is absent, which changes the normaliser. For critics the per-cell generator weight is proportional to 1/n_k; for the discriminator it is uniform. Batch weights are therefore 1/K vs π_k, which confounds critic-vs-discriminator contrasts on unbalanced tasks.
evidence: Batch fractions from prepped obs (atac_small and immune from the pilot prep; other datasets from the 2026-08-25 prep, same cells): immune smart-seq2 averages 3.9 cells per minibatch (P(absent)=0.019), and its per-cell weight is 12.6× that of v2_10X; pancreas smallest batch 5.0 cells (P=0.006, ratio 5.7×); atac_large smallest 5.5 cells (P=0.0035, ratio 17.4×). Reference-batch cells per minibatch: pancreas 15.1, sim1 18.6, atac_large 26.3.
reviewer_risk: Results §2 (multi-batch scalability and stability): poor critic scaling may be estimator variance from too few cells per head, not a property of W1.
recommendation: Turn claim 4 into a mechanism test: report n_k per minibatch, and on the multi-batch tasks add a balanced-sampling robustness arm (at least m cells per batch per minibatch, or heads weighted by π_k).

title: The adversary optimiser and step counts match neither WGAN-GP/WDGRL nor scvi-tools' adversarial classifier
location: scripts/scvi_adversarial_plan.py:197 (opt_d = Adam(lr=1e-3, betas=(0.5,0.9))), :240 (disc_iter loop on one z sample); src/wcd_vae/wcd/adversarial.py:36 (128×2 MLP head)
description: Critics use Adam lr 1e-3, β=(0.5,0.9), eps 1e-8, no weight decay, n_critic=10, and the same minibatch for every critic step. The discriminator uses the same optimiser and head, fixed λ, and 1 or 10 steps.
evidence: WGAN-GP Alg. 1 defaults: λ=10, n_critic=5, α=1e-4, β1=0, β2=0.9, fresh samples at each critic iteration. WDGRL: critic lr 1e-4, n=5, γ=10, one minibatch reused across critic steps (Alg. 1, lines 3-5). WGAN: RMSProp 5e-5, n_critic=5, weight clipping. scvi-tools 1.4.2 AdversarialTrainingPlan: Classifier(n_hidden=32, n_layers=2, batch norm, dropout 0.1), Adam(lr=1e-3, eps=0.01, wd=1e-6), one step after the generator step, loss weight κ=1−kl_weight.
reviewer_risk: R3.2 (robustness to architecture and hyperparameters) and the 'scVI as people use it' framing: the discriminator arm is not scvi-tools' stock adversarial scVI, and the critic learning rate is 10× the WGAN-GP default.
recommendation: In the original hyperparameter-sensitivity section, add, on 2-3 datasets, one critic setting at WGAN-GP defaults and one discriminator arm that is exactly scvi-tools' adversarial_classifier=True (with the κ schedule). Document the shared head as the controlled design.

title: A fixed λ is applied against a KL warm-up that never completes on the large datasets
location: scvi TrainingPlan n_epochs_kl_warmup=400 × the epoch heuristic; scripts/scvi_adversarial_plan.py (fixed d_coef from step 0)
description: The final kl_weight is (epochs−1)/400: immune 0.595 (239 epochs), lung 0.68 (273), immune_hum_mou 0.23 (92), atac_large 0.23 (94), all others about 1.0. The adversary runs at full λ from epoch 0 while KL is near 0, unlike DANN (λ ramped from 0 to 1) and scvi-tools (κ = 1−kl_weight). W1 scales with the latent scale, which the KL ramp sets, while cross-entropy is scale-invariant. The effective strength of critics relative to the discriminator therefore drifts during training and differs between datasets.
evidence: scvi 1.4.2 _compute_kl_weight (epoch-based, slope·epoch/400) and get_max_epochs_heuristic (min(round(20000/n·400), 400)). DANN text: λ_p = 2/(1+exp(−10p))−1. Cell numbers after prep for lung and immune_hum_mou come from the 2026-08-25 prep and are PROVISIONAL, because these datasets do not prep at 5709a98 (N10). The arm dependence is inferred from W1's scaling with the latent scale, not measured.
reviewer_risk: Results §3 (λ sensitivity): one shared λ grid means different adversary strengths on different datasets and arms.
recommendation: Report the final kl_weight per dataset. On 2 datasets, run a robustness check with the warm-up completed (n_epochs_kl_warmup ≤ max_epochs), logging critic gap and latent RMS per epoch (N15).

title: The baselines break the same-epochs/batch/latent rule, and scANVI is trained on the evaluation labels

description: The scVI baseline uses 30 latent dimensions and at most 200 epochs with early stopping on the 10% validation split; the arms use 10 dimensions, heuristic epochs and no early stopping. scANVI is warm-started from that scVI and trained 100 more epochs with labels_key=celltype and unlabeled_category='Unknown'. Harmony, Scanorama and PCA ignore the seed (prior M6, unchanged). fit_stock_scvi.py (pilot) is the only rule-compliant scVI.

reviewer_risk: R2.4/R3.1: the 'adversary vs scVI' comparison and the ranking figure compare unequal budgets and dimensions, and scANVI's bio advantage comes from the labels by construction.

Per the rule, give PCA/Harmony/Scanorama 10 dimensions (10 PCA components), with the tool-default 50-dimension run as a sensitivity check. Note in Methods that PCR comparison uses the prep's 50-PC X_pca as the 'before' state. Report deterministic baselines once, without seed CIs.

title: scIB-native scoring: scaled scores depend on the comparison set, and organism, trajectory and clustering protocol need fixing
description: (i) scib_overall min-max scales within each dataset across whatever rows are in the frame, so adding or removing collapsed high-λ configs or baselines changes every config's overall score. NaN metrics are skipped per row, so different rows can average different metric sets. (ii) ORGANISM defaults to 'human', which is wrong for the mouse ATAC data, and the Splatter sims have no cell-cycle genes. (iii) Trajectory conservation is omitted although immune and immune_hum_mou carry obs['dpt_pseudotime']. (iv) scib 1.1.7's cluster_optimal_resolution runs Leiden at 10 resolutions (0.2-2.0), not the paper's Louvain at 0.1-2.0 in steps of 0.1.
evidence: Re-scored the pilot's 58 'new' rows with the committed scib_overall (no refits). Removing the λ≥20 rows from the scaling set changed per-config overall scores by −0.008 to +0.017 and reordered the five arms that lie within 0.633-0.646. cell_cycle was NaN in all 58 rows (ORGANISM=none). scib source: get_resolutions(n=10, max=2), cluster_function=sc.tl.leiden. scIB paper Methods: min-max scaling within a task; Louvain at 0.1-2. h5py: dpt_pseudotime is present in Immune_ALL_human.h5ad and Immune_ALL_hum_mou.h5ad.
reviewer_risk: Near-tie claims and the baseline ranking can flip with the comparison set. R1.minor.2 and R3.minor.2 ask for trajectory evidence that the data already support.
recommendation: Pre-declare one comparison set per dataset (all fixed-grid configs plus baselines, both decoders) and use it for every figure. Also report raw metrics, and require complete metric vectors. Set ORGANISM per dataset (mouse for ATAC, none for the sims). Enable trajectory_ for immune and immune_hum_mou. State the scib 1.1.7 clustering grid in Methods.

title: The Sinkhorn arm uses a squared-Euclidean cost, so it is not the critic-free counterpart of the W1 critic
description: Entropic OT with cost ‖x−y‖² approximates W2², not W1 (whose cost is ‖x−y‖), and MMD is a different IPM. The module docstring's 'keeps the geometry and drops the adversary' therefore does not hold for W1. The detached scale (prior H2) is unchanged.
evidence: Code reading: _pdist2 returns cdist(p=2)**2, and the docstring itself says 'squared-Euclidean ground cost'.
reviewer_risk: R2.1/R2.3, if the critic-free arms are used to argue about the adversarial estimator.
recommendation: If the critic-free arms are kept, use a p=1 (Euclidean) cost for a W1-matched arm, or describe Sinkhorn and MMD as different geometries.
